papers.title: A Heterogeneous Multi-Modal Parallel Deep Learning Framework for Multiaxial Fatigue Life Prediction of Metals
papers.abstract: Multiaxial fatigue damage remains a critical barrier to the reliable design of metallic engineering components, particularly under complex non-proportional loading paths. Conventional critical-plane and energy-based models rely heavily on empirical assumptions and struggle to capture intricate path-dependent damage evolution, leading to limited accuracy and generalizability. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel data-driven framework that integrates heterogeneous information sources through a three-branch parallel neural architecture. Specifically, a deep neural network (DNN) extracts static material intrinsic properties; a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) enhanced with a multi-head self-attention mechanism captures long-term temporal dependencies and adaptively weights key stages in loading histories; and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) extracts local strain fluctuation patterns. The three streams are fused to produce a comprehensive damage representation for end-to-end life prediction. The output of the model is the base −10 logarithm of fatigue life, i.e., lg(Nf). Evaluated on a public multiaxial fatigue dataset comprising 40 metals and 1167 samples, the proposed model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9052, achieving promising performance on a fixed data split (R2 = 0.9052); ablation studies demonstrate the complementary nature of the three feature extraction branches, though 5-fold cross-validation suggests that the performance gain requires further validation with larger datasets. Systematic ablation studies confirm that the multi-source fusion strategy and the attention mechanism are pivotal to the performance gain. This work offers a robust and effective data-driven solution for high-accuracy fatigue life assessment, and points toward future integration of physical knowledge to further enhance extrapolation and transparency.

papers.title: Blockchain Architecture Vulnerabilities: A Multi-Approach Analysis of Critical Systems
papers.abstract: Blockchain systems face critical security vulnerabilities across all architectural layers, with over $1.8 billion stolen in 2023 alone. This systematic review analyzes 140 peer-reviewed studies (2018–2025) to provide a comprehensive taxonomy of blockchain vulnerabilities, detection methods, and mitigation strategies. We categorize 30+ distinct attack types across five architectural layers (Hardware, Data, Network, Consensus, Application) and three critical applications (Smart Contracts, Decentralized Exchanges, Supply Chains). Our quantitative analysis reveals severe research imbalance: the Application layer receives 58% of research attention with 45+ detection tools, while foundational Hardware (9%) and Data layers (6.7%) remain critically underexplored. We systematically compare 25+ vulnerability detection tools, identifying their strengths, limitations, and deployment contexts. Unlike existing surveys focusing on isolated aspects, we provide integrated detection mitigation mappings and analyze vulnerability propagation across layers. We identify nine security paradigms including AI-powered agents, zero-knowledge proofs, and post-quantum cryptography with assessment of maturity levels and adoption timelines. This work provides researchers and practitioners with an actionable roadmap for understanding current vulnerabilities, selecting appropriate tools, and anticipating future challenges in blockchain ecosystems.

papers.title: Adaptive Modality Routing for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting with Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: Temporal knowledge graph forecasting aims to predict future missing facts from continuously evolving relational data in dynamic information systems. Such forecasting tasks are increasingly important for intelligent applications involving complex interactions among entities, events, and evolving environments. Existing approaches typically employ unified architectures that process all queries through the same representation pipeline, despite substantial variations in structural connectivity, historical availability, and semantic information among different queries. Such a homogeneous modeling strategy may limit the ability to effectively handle diverse forecasting scenarios, including highly connected entities, recurrent temporal patterns, and cold-start cases with insufficient historical evidence. To address this challenge, we propose a Heterogeneous Modality Mixture-of-Experts (H-MoE) framework that adaptively selects specialized reasoning pathways according to query characteristics. Unlike conventional mixture-of-experts architectures with homogeneous subnetworks, our framework incorporates three complementary experts with distinct inductive biases: a time-aware graph neural network for structural relational reasoning, a temporal transformer for historical sequence modeling, and a semantic representation adapter based on pretrained language models for knowledge transfer in sparse scenarios. A query-aware gating network is introduced to dynamically allocate computational resources among different experts according to the available structural, temporal, and semantic evidence. Furthermore, we employ entropy-based routing regularization to encourage confident expert selection while maintaining balanced expert utilization, together with a representation diversity constraint to promote complementary feature learning among heterogeneous reasoning pathways. Experiments on three benchmark temporal knowledge graph datasets indicate that the proposed framework can improve forecasting performance under the evaluation setting used in this study. The largest observed gains occur for queries with limited historical evidence. These findings support heterogeneous expert specialization as a useful design direction, while the scope of the conclusions remains limited to the tested ICEWS benchmarks and implementation.

papers.title: FADLinear: A Compression-Aware Linear Architecture Evaluated for Temperature-Oriented Long-Horizon Forecasting
papers.abstract: Temperature-oriented long-horizon forecasting requires stable extrapolation of slowly evolving targets in the presence of local fluctuations and instance-level distribution shifts. This paper presents FADLinear, a target-only linear forecasting architecture evaluated on temperature-oriented tasks. The term “temperature-oriented” describes the empirical scope; the architecture itself remains domain-generic. FADLinear applies reversible instance normalization to the designated target, extracts a constrained Gaussian-like low-pass trend before stride-2 compression, constructs a full-resolution residual path, and combines two linear branch forecasts through bounded energy-contrast calibration. The evaluation compares eight models over 30 public dataset–horizon tasks and uses three random seeds to stabilize each task estimate. Task means for the statistical analyses are calculated from seed-level metrics before four-decimal table display. Friedman and paired Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction summarize the observed, partially dependent benchmark suite: lower FADLinear error is detected relative to four baselines for MSE and six baselines for MAE, while no difference is detected relative to PatchTST for either metric. Descriptively, FADLinear is best or tied for best on 8 MSE tasks and 10 MAE tasks, with mean ranks of 2.433 and 2.233. In the controlled ETTh1 efficiency benchmark at L=336 and H=720, FADLinear uses 0.365 million parameters and 0.750 million FLOPs per target forecast, with 0.890 ms median batch-1 latency and 9.58 MiB peak inference memory. These results support a top-tier accuracy–efficiency trade-off rather than universal accuracy superiority. An ETTm2-derived stress test is retained only for exploratory characterization because its construction does not satisfy split-first causal isolation.

papers.title: A Novel Hybrid Grey Wolf–Whale Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Optimization of a Terahertz Antenna for Future Communications
papers.abstract: A novel hybrid metaheuristic optimization algorithm for antenna design optimization is presented in this paper. The proposed algorithm, called the Hybrid Grey Wolf–Whale Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm (HGWWOA-PSO), combines the exploration capability of Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), the exploitation mechanism of the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and the adaptive search strategy of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to solve a multi-objective antenna design problem. The proposed hybrid algorithm is evaluated and validated based on its convergence characteristics and distribution of cost function value in comparison with GWO and WOA. The proposed HGWWOA-PSO is used to optimize the reflection coefficient, gain, and radiation efficiency of a terahertz antenna with a footprint of 0.24λo × 0.24λo at 361 GHz. The optimization targets three resonant frequencies (361 GHz, 391.6 GHz, and 611.2 GHz). The optimized antenna has a reflection coefficient of −51.35 dB, −16.7 dB, and −20 dB at 361.0 GHz, 391.6 GHz, and 611.2 GHz, respectively. The resonances at 361.0 GHz and 391.6 GHz combine to form a lower operating band, hence a dual-band antenna. The lower operating band achieves a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 56.21 GHz (347.34–403.55 GHz), while the upper band impedance bandwidth is 183.21 GHz (524.60–707.81 GHz). The peak gain and radiation efficiency achieved are 4.5 dBi and 95%, respectively, while maintaining an omnidirectional radiation pattern in the E-plane and H-plane across both operating bands. The combination of miniaturization, multiband capability, high gain, and high radiation efficiency makes the proposed antenna an attractive candidate for terahertz communication systems.
